I like the view of http://localhost:3000/analysis with all intuitiveness and ease of use, but the http://localhost:3000/situation provides more enriched data from various sources. Combine both of them to the http://localhost:3000/situation page. What I like from the UI: Less text, highlighting for feedback cases. The current http://localhost:3000/situation page is too crowded with text and less of important indicators. For example: [<div class="group/card f..." data-slot="card" data-size="default" /> in DataCoverage (at src/app/(dashboard)/situation/[derivate]/page.tsx:222:5) in Card (at src/components/ui/card.tsx:10:5) in CarView (at src/app/(dashboard)/situation/[derivate]/page.tsx:130:9) in SituationCarPage (at src/app/(dashboard)/situation/[derivate]/page.tsx:55:7)] is too verbose. Think of some charts to summarize the overall data. Also Hygience Factor  for assesment column is not a clear word.
I'm in plan mode, so I should explore the codebase first, looking at the analysis page and situation page by reading the key files directly instead of using a separate agent.

parts.text:
I'm thinking through whether merging into /situation means removing /analysis entirely, or whether the situation page should absorb analysis-style KPIs like feedback count, net sentiment, problem share, priority charts, and verbatim highlighting, while keeping analysis queries scoped by derivate, country, and engine.

I need to figure out how region (EU/US/CN) maps to ISO country codes in feedback entries, and whether there's a market column I'm missing in the schema. I'm also unsure if "highlighting" refers to the `<mark>` quote snippet styling from analysis or just color-coding cases by sentiment direction -- I should ask for clarification.

parts.text:
I should assign explicit colors to the chart config instead of relying on greyscale defaults, and I'm figuring out how the quote source ids map to feedback entries so highlighting can join correctly through feedback aspects. Now I'm ready to put together the plan.

For the layout, I'll put the engine selector in the Customer voice card header to avoid confusion, since it only affects feedback-related data. The page will open with a KPI strip of four concise cards: feedback count with net sentiment, percentage with a problem, requirements count out of total features, and an evidence status indicator with tooltips replacing the old data coverage section. Below that, a charts row will show feature verdicts as a single stacked chart replacing several old KPIs and the legend, plus a horizontal bar chart for requirements by category.

Clicking a category bar will set a URL filter instead of using a pill selector, which means making that chart a client component for the click handler. The requirements table gets slimmed down to essentials — feature, verdict, target, and customer problem percentage — dropping the long statement and description text. I'll add a customer voice card showing top VFC categories by priority alongside top strengths, clickable into a shared aspect detail sheet, and replace the other features table with clickable chips grouped by verdict, plus a footer run line and colored quote borders in the feature sheet based on sentiment direction.

I'm figuring out how to join analysis quotes to feedback aspects so I can highlight the matching verbatim snippet in the sheet, and considering whether to lightly touch the /situation index page too, even though the user's complaint was mainly about the car detail page — I'll include it as an optional step. For code reuse, I'll move Verbatim, AspectDetail, Bar, and Kpi into shared components so both /analysis and /situation can use them without changing /analysis's existing behavior. On the server side, I'm considering extending the Scope type to support multiple countries instead of just one.

I think I can simplify this by adding an optional `countries` array field to Scope, moving the EU27 list to a shared lib file, and updating the `inScope` check to allow for null or array membership — US maps to `["US"]`, EU maps to EU27, and ALL/CN map to null since there's no CN feedback. I also want to rename "hygiene_factor" to "Must-have" across the assessment labels, chat instructions, and any literal text appearing in requirement statements, doing a simple regex replace at display time in the sheet.

For the chart dependency, I'll pull in shadcn's chart component which brings recharts, checking if it also drags in lucide-react so I can swap that for hugeicons, then commit the lockfile. I'll work in a dedicated worktree per AGENTS.md conventions, validate with lint/format/build/test, and do a visual check across the G60, G68, and F70 views in both light and dark mode, keeping in mind G68 will show empty states since there's no feedback data there.

I have a plan for the merged `/situation/[derivate]` page. Nothing has been changed yet; this is read-only so far. You've chosen to keep `/analysis` as it is, rename "Hygiene factor" to **Must-have**, use shadcn Chart (which adds recharts), and scope customer feedback by the page's market plus an engine filter.

## New layout of `/situation/[derivate]`

| # | Block | Replaces | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Header | — | Car code, name and segment, plus the market pills (All/EU/US/CN). |
| 1 | KPI strip with 4 cards: one big number and one short caption each, no paragraphs | The 4 current KPI cards | **Feedback** (count and net sentiment, e.g. "Good +0.13"), **Feedback with a problem** (%), **Requirements** ("11 of 74 features"), **Evidence**: one coloured dot each for Our model, Competitors, Customers and Trends; hovering shows what is missing; caption "3 of 4 complete". This replaces the wordy `DataCoverage` card. |
| 2a | Chart **Feature verdicts** | The "Gaps · demands" and "Features analysed" cards, and the Legend at the bottom | One stacked bar of all features: Gap / Demand / Must-have / Strength / Unclear. The legend shows counts and each label's meaning appears on hover. |
| 2b | Chart **Requirements by category** | The category pill filter | A horizontal bar chart stacked by verdict. Clicking a bar sets `?category`, with a "clear" link next to it. |
| 3 | **Recommended requirements**, slimmed down | The current wide table | Columns: # · Feature (category in small grey text) · Verdict badge · Target · Customer problems as a bar plus %. The long requirement text column is dropped; the full statement stays in the side sheet. The description shrinks to one line. |
| 4 | **Customer voice** (from /analysis) | — | A chart of the top 8 categories by priority (red bars, reach × severity) and the top 3 strengths (green). The Engine dropdown sits in this card's header, because runs are not split by engine. Clicking a category opens the aspect sheet with the highlighted verbatims from /analysis. |
| 5 | **Other assessed features** | The 5-column table | Chips grouped by verdict, each one clickable, with a one-line note that these are rule-based and low certainty. |
| 6 | Footer | — | The run id line, unchanged. |

In the **feature side sheet**, customer quotes get a coloured left border for problem, request and praise. The aspect's quote snippet is highlighted with `<mark>`, the same way /analysis does it. The snippet comes from joining `analysis_quotes.source_id` to `feedback_entries.feedback_explorer_id` and then to `feedback_aspects.quote_snippet`.

## Changes by file

- **Charts:** `pnpm dlx shadcn add chart` adds `src/components/ui/chart.tsx` and recharts. The registry lists lucide-react as a dependency; if it gets pulled in, I'll switch its icons to hugeicons. Chart colours are set explicitly (destructive red, sky, amber, emerald), because the theme's `--chart-*` colours are greyscale. Small client components go in `src/components/situation/charts.tsx`.
- **Shared code moved, /analysis unchanged:**
  - `Verbatim`, `AspectDetail`, `Bar` and `Kpi` move out of `analysis/[derivate]/page.tsx` into `src/components/feedback/*`.
  - Both pages import them from there. /analysis looks and behaves the same.
- **Feedback scoped by market:**
  - `Scope` in `src/server/analysis/queries.ts` gets an optional `countries?: string[]`, and `inScope` adds `e.country = any(...)`.
  - `EU27` moves from `src/server/chat/lib.ts` to `src/lib`.
  - Market mapping: All = no filter, EU = EU27, US = `["US"]`, CN = `["CN"]`.
  - Existing callers of `Scope` don't change.
- **Highlighted quotes:** the quotes query in `src/server/situation/queries.ts` gets a `left join` that returns `snippets`.
- **Must-have:**
  - The label and hint change in `ASSESSMENTS` (`src/components/situation/parts.tsx`).
  - `SITUATION_INSTRUCTIONS` gets one line so the chat also says "Must-have".
  - Some stored requirement texts literally contain `hygiene_factor`. They are replaced at display time in the sheet; the stored data is not touched.
- **Index page `/situation`:** each region row becomes a badge, a small verdict bar and the requirement count. The "#1 recommendation" paragraph is cut to the feature name on a single line.

## How I'll work and check it

- All work happens in a worktree, `.worktrees/situation-merge`, on branch `feat/situation-merge`, as AGENTS.md requires.
- Checks: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm fmt:check`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm build`.
- Visual check with Playwright on port 3001:
  - G60 under All, EU and US, plus F70.
  - G68 under CN, which has no feedback, to see the empty "Customer voice" state.
  - Both sheets and dark mode.
- Afterwards I commit with the lockfile and open a PR.

## Two open points

1. **The index page change:** is it in scope? Your feedback was about the car page.
2. **Requirements table:** should each row keep a one-line requirement title, truncated, or show no requirement text at all, as planned above?

Reply "go" with your answers to these two and I'll start.

parts.text:
I'm noticing snippets only cover a small fraction of quotes, so highlighting based on them will be sparse. I'll fall back on the colored border grouping by direction as the main feedback indicator, using snippets as a supplement when they exist.

I'll build a shared Highlighted component that marks matching snippets (case-insensitive) within quote text, reused by Verbatim, filtering snippets loosely by sentiment tone relative to the direction. Writing the SQL aggregation query...

Now I'm planning the overall file structure: updating markets.ts, queries, and chat lib for EU27 scope handling, adding snippet support to the situation queries, and extracting shared feedback components like Bar, Kpi, Verbatim, AspectDetail, and Stat from the analysis page.

I'm weighing whether to split these into separate files or consolidate into one shared module like `src/components/feedback.tsx`, since AspectDetail is an async server component that imports server-only queries while the rest are pure presentational pieces, and I want to avoid duplicating the hrefWith helper across pages.

I'll reuse the Stat component from situation/parts since it's identical to the analysis version, and unify the two Kpi variants by taking the more flexible analysis one and adding an evidence slot elsewhere. Now I'm thinking through the charts module, specifically whether the VerdictBar stacked bar visualization actually needs recharts or could be done with simple divs.

Deciding instead to use recharts selectively—for the requirements-by-category and customer-voice-priority bar charts since those add clickability value—while rendering the verdict overview as a donut chart with a centered total count and legend, since that's a more iconic summary visual than a single stacked bar.

For the customer voice bar chart, I'm weighing whether to size bars by priority score or by reach percentage; reach is more intuitive to read ("7.4% report a problem"), but ordering by priority while sizing by reach could look non-monotonic and confusing, so I need to settle on consistent ordering and keep severity/demand/net details in the tooltip to minimize on-chart text.

Actually, a diverging bar design — red for complaint share, green for praise share per category — feels stronger since it merges the "improve" and "strengths" views into one chart, and clicking a bar can open the detailed aspect sheet filtered by tone. I'll show the top 10 categories by priority rather than all 15 to keep the chart compact, with the full breakdown still available on the detailed analysis page.

I'm sketching the diverging bar chart structure: plotting problem reach as negative values and praise as positive values with a sign-based stack offset, labeling categories on the vertical axis, and formatting the axis ticks as absolute percentages. Clicking a bar routes to the relevant category/tone href, computed server-side and passed down as props, with the client using the router to navigate without scrolling.

For the stacked verdict bars, I'm making each category clickable to filter by that category, dimming non-active bars via cell opacity rather than removing them. The verdict donut chart gets a center label showing the total, a custom legend below listing counts, and it respects the active category filter so key figures stay scoped to the selection.

Now I'm laying out the requirements table columns -- id, feature with category tag, verdict, a truncated single-line requirement with a tooltip for the full text, target, and a mini problem-reach bar with percentage.

For truncation I'm using the `w-full max-w-0` trick on the table cell so the column absorbs remaining width and the text inside truncates cleanly with a title attribute for the full string. Since requirement text often starts with a repetitive "The successor should improve..." prefix that eats into the visible truncated text, I'm stripping that prefix via regex and bolding the actual intent instead.

I'm also planning the problems section with a share bar visualization, the "other features" chips grouped by verdict type with color coding, and an evidence card showing completeness dots across model, competitors, customers, and trends sources.

For missing-info indicators I'll keep it simple with a title attribute rather than a fancy tooltip component, and drop the explanatory hover text per the user's feedback. Then I'm defining the KPI cards: feedback count with mood coloring, percentage of feedback tied to a problem with the top complaint category as a hint, and requirements coverage showing count out of total features analyzed.

For evidence I'll show source completeness as dots like "3/4 sources complete." The engine dropdown reuses ScopeSelect pulling global engine options, placed in the Customer voice card header alongside the market pills. I also need to handle the aspect and feature sheets sharing URL params, making sure only one sheet is open at a time and that clicking a region pill clears the aspect selection too, plus wiring up verbatim actions like attaching feedback to chat.

On situation pages, chat already carries region context without an engine param, so I'll leave that alone, and I'll skip adding crumbs there since only analysis pages need them. For the index page, I'm adding a mini verdict bar per car card built from stacked CSS segments, which means pulling verdict counts per run via a new jsonb aggregation query grouping assessments by run.

I'll extend the RunSummary type with a verdicts record, and also add a topFeature field that resolves the label behind the #1 requirement rather than just the raw statement. Car cards can also surface feedback count and net sentiment from listCars for a richer summary line like "4,000 feedback · Good."

For verdict colors, I'm mapping each verdict type to a CSS color variable, but I need to double check whether Tailwind v4 actually emits those theme color vars by default or only when the class is used elsewhere.

For the muted bar fill I'll settle on a color-mix expression blending muted-foreground at 30% opacity. Since parts.tsx has no server-only restriction, importing ASSESSMENTS into client chart components works fine. I also need to update the "Must-have" label hint text, tweak the chat instructions to mention it's shown as "Must-have" in the UI, and replace "hygiene_factor" wording in the displayed requirement text.

For the feature sheet quotes, I'm adding colored left borders to indicate direction—destructive for problems, sky for requests, emerald for strengths, muted for neutral—and keeping the rest of the sheet layout as is since that wasn't flagged for simplification. Now I'm checking what data fetches the situation page needs: run details, features, regions, and car listings for naming.

For G68 with no feedback data, I'm confirming the ranking returns an empty total that gracefully falls back to zero from the summary, so the empty state renders correctly. I'm also verifying the customer voice feedback derivate codes align with the model codes, and checking card.tsx for the CardAction pattern already used elsewhere in the repo.

parts.text:
I'm now setting up the client-side charts file, starting with a donut chart component that visualizes verdict counts with a center label and an accompanying legend.

I'll map verdict keys to colors via a chart config so each pie slice and bar segment pulls its fill from a CSS variable, then move to the horizontal stacked bar chart for category breakdowns, wiring up row clicks to navigate to each row's href and adding hover/active styling.

I'm sizing the chart dynamically based on row count and embedding the item count directly into each Y-axis label rather than fighting with label positioning on zero-width bar segments. Now I'm starting on the VoiceChart component, which will show problem/praise fractions per row with their own hrefs and counts.

For this diverging bar chart I'm setting up a vertical layout with signed stacking so problem percentages go negative and praise percentages go positive, using a zero reference line and custom tooltip formatting to show absolute percentages alongside raw counts.

Since the formatter replaces the whole tooltip row I'll manually add a colored indicator square, and I'm adding a small legend caption above the chart distinguishing complaints from praise, plus click handlers that navigate to the corresponding problem or praise detail pages, keeping all server-passed props as plain serializable objects.

Setting bar radii for the diverging chart and sizing the Y-axis wide enough for long category labels while hiding default tick and axis lines.

Writing the car view page component...

Pulling in the run data, scope options, feature summary, and ranking in parallel, then wiring up aspect selection and tone logic for the ranking rows, with the fallback region defaulting to the first available run when none is specified in search params.

I'm sketching out the KPI row showing customer feedback count alongside a colored mood indicator (good/bad sentiment with signed delta), passing the mood label as a styled hint element rather than plain text.

I'm adding more KPIs for problem-feedback percentage with the top category called out, recommended requirement counts scoped to analyzed features, and an evidence KPI component, then thinking about whether the engine filter should be reflected in these feedback hints since the engine selector lives in the customer voice card.

Since the engine filter affects the feedback KPIs but not the requirements one, I decide it's clearer to move the engine select up to the header near the market pills rather than tucking it into the customer voice card, and I'll label it "Feedback engine" to keep it short and unambiguous about its scope.

I'm renaming the "Region" label to "Market" for consistency, then writing the EvidenceKpi component, which tallies how many agents have an "ok" status and renders a KPI with a dot-indicator list for each agent.

For the layout below, I'm planning row two as a two-column grid: a "Feature verdicts" card showing the VerdictDonut, and a "Requirements by category" card with a clearable filter and a CategoryChart (or an empty-state message), stacking verdict counts across requirement categories. Row three will hold a slimmed-down RequirementsTable.

For row four, I'm adding a "Customer voice" card describing feedback sentiment per category, with a link to the full ranking page and a bar chart (or empty-state text if no feedback exists). I'm working out which rows to include by combining the top eight by priority with the top three by positive sentiment, deduplicating and reordering by priority.

For the sheets, I'm figuring out how feature and aspect detail panels interact—selecting one should clear the other's query param, with feature taking priority if both are set. Then I'm laying out the requirements table with columns for feature, verdict, requirement text, target, and a problems bar chart, making sure the requirement cell truncates properly within a constrained width while the feature name stays on one line.

Since the whole row is clickable via an overlay link, I realize the title tooltip on the truncated paragraph won't be reachable—so I'm moving the title attribute to the Link itself so hovering anywhere in the row shows the full requirement text. Now I'm building the "Other assessed features" card with its description noting these are rule-based and less certain, plus a note about how many had insufficient evidence.

Writing feature chip rows...

For the index page, I'll need listCars to include feedback counts and net scores, then build each car row with a verdict badge, a VerdictStrip showing proportional CSS segments for each assessment category, and the requirement count, followed by a top-feature line. I'm now defining the VerdictStrip server component itself, computing totals across verdict keys (folding not_assessed into unclear) and rendering a thin rounded bar with a tooltip listing counts per category.

I should also add a compact legend near the title on the index page using a VerdictLegend component showing colored dots with labels -- cheap but useful. For the feature-detail view, I'll apply quote highlighting and jargon-simplification to the statement, reasoning, whatExactly, and facts fields, including unjargon-ing the citation reasoning text, and map rule suggestions like "hygiene_factor" through the ASSESSMENTS labels. Next I'll move on to writing charts.tsx.

The YAxis labels are wrapping unexpectedly—"Powertrain & Performance" breaks across lines while similarly-sized labels don't, likely due to recharts' text width estimation on category ticks. I'll fix this by replacing the default tick rendering with a custom tick function that draws plain text without wrapping, applied to both charts.

I also want to tweak the percentage formatter so a zero value shows "0" instead of "0.0%", and I'm checking layout balance between the feature verdicts and requirements cards, plus confirming the recommended requirements truncation and zero-demand display look fine before moving on to the dev issue.

parts.text:
The `/situation` page now combines both views: the deep situation data plus the charts and highlighted feedback from `/analysis`. It's in PR https://github.com/itsmeyaw/bmwow/pull/18, on branch `feat/situation-merge` (worktree `.worktrees/situation-merge`). `/analysis` is unchanged. Lint, formatting, tests and build pass. I clicked through G60 (All, EU, US, with a category filter), G70 in dark mode, G68 CN (which has no feedback), both side sheets, and `/analysis`.

**Car page (`/situation/G60` etc.)**
- **Summary cards:** one number per card with a short caption:
  - customer feedback count and sentiment;
  - share of feedback with a problem, with the top category;
  - number of recommended requirements;
  - "Evidence complete: 3 of 4" with four coloured dots. Hovering a dot shows what is missing. This replaces the wordy evidence card you pointed at.
- **Feature verdicts:** a donut chart with counts per verdict; hovering a label shows what it means.
- **Requirements by category:** stacked bars per category. Clicking a bar filters the page to that category.
- **Requirements table:** fewer columns. The requirement text is cut to one line, with the full text on hover and in the side sheet. Each row has a small bar for the share of customers reporting a problem.
- **Customer voice (from `/analysis`):** complaints and praise per category, side by side. Clicking a bar opens the same verbatim panel as on `/analysis`, with the quote highlighted.
- **Other assessed features:** clickable chips grouped by verdict, instead of a table.
- **Market and engine:** customer feedback follows the selected market (All, EU, US, CN). There's also a new "Feedback engine" dropdown in the header; it only filters customer feedback, because the requirement runs aren't split by engine.

**Feature side panel**
- Customer quotes have a coloured left border: red for problems, blue for requests, green for praise.
- The relevant phrase in each quote is highlighted, but only where the feedback data has one. Few quotes do (166 of 1,116), so most show only the border.

**Overview page (`/situation`)**
- Each market row shows a small coloured bar of the verdicts and its requirement count.
- Each car shows its feedback count, its sentiment and its #1 feature on one line.

**"Hygiene factor"** is now shown as **"Must-have"** everywhere, including in stored texts and in the chat's answers. The data itself is unchanged.

The charts add one dependency, recharts (via shadcn's chart component).

The worktree is still there; I'll remove it after the PR merges if you confirm.
